text: Which of the following best distinguishes 'commerce' from 'trade' in business studies?
options: Commerce includes trade plus all auxiliaries like transport and insurance; trade is the buying and selling of goods only.
Commerce is only concerned with export and import while trade deals with local buying and selling.
Commerce is the study of company law while trade refers to professional occupations.
Commerce and trade are the same and the terms are completely interchangeable.
explanation: Commerce is broader than trade: it covers trade (buying and selling) plus auxiliary services such as transport, warehousing, insurance, banking and advertising that facilitate exchange and distribution of goods and services.
subject: Commerce

text: Which of the following is NOT an auxiliary service of commerce?
explanation: Auxiliary services support the flow of goods from producer to consumer; manufacturing is a production activity, not an auxiliary service that facilitates trade or distribution.
subject: Commerce

text: Which type of wholesaler specializes in buying large quantities from producers and breaking them into small lots for retailers?
explanation: Bulk-breaking wholesalers purchase in bulk from producers and subdivide into consignments suitable for retailers; this function helps match producer output with retailer demand and aids distribution.
subject: Commerce

text: Which document issued by a carrier acknowledges receipt of goods for shipment and can act as a document of title?
explanation: A bill of lading is issued by the carrier upon receiving goods for shipment; it acknowledges receipt, details shipment terms and can serve as a document of title enabling transfer of ownership.
subject: Commerce

text: Which term describes a trade contract where the seller bears the cost, insurance and freight to the buyer's port?
explanation: CIF means the seller pays cost, insurance and freight to bring goods to the buyer's named port; the seller arranges and pays transport and insurance to that destination.
subject: Commerce

text: Under marine insurance, which principle states that an insured should not profit from a loss but be placed in the same financial position as before the loss?
explanation: The principle of indemnity ensures an insured is compensated to restore them to the financial position before the loss, preventing profiteering from insurance claims and maintaining fairness.
subject: Commerce

text: When a cheque is crossed generally with 'Account Payee Only', this crossing implies that the cheque will be:
options: Paid only at the counter to the bearer
Paid into the account of the payee named on the cheque
Endorsable and transferable by any holder
Payable only in cash at any bank
explanation: An 'Account Payee Only' crossing restricts payment to the bank account of the named payee, preventing negotiation or payment to a bearer and enhancing security of the cheque transaction.
subject: Commerce

text: Which of the following is the best advantage of e-commerce for small businesses?
options: Lower entry cost and wider market access
explanation: E-commerce lowers entry costs by removing the need for large physical premises and enables small businesses to reach broader markets online, increasing customer access and potential sales opportunities.
subject: Commerce

text: Which characteristic is typical of a sole proprietorship?
options: Single owner who bears unlimited liability
Owned by many shareholders with transferable shares
explanation: A sole proprietorship is owned by one person who has unlimited liability, meaning personal assets can be used to settle business debts; it is not a separate legal entity from the owner.
subject: Commerce

text: Which of the following correctly contrasts a partnership from a limited liability company?
options: Partners have limited liability; company owners have unlimited liability.
Partnerships are governed by company law; limited companies are informal agreements.
Partners typically have unlimited liability; company shareholders have limited liability.
Partnerships always have more capital than limited companies.
explanation: In a partnership, partners often have unlimited liability exposing personal assets to business debts, while shareholders of a limited liability company are liable only to the extent of unpaid shares, protecting personal assets.
subject: Commerce

text: Which of the following is a defining feature of a cooperative society?
explanation: Cooperatives operate on democratic principles where each member typically has one vote regardless of capital contribution. They focus on member welfare rather than maximizing profits for external shareholders.
subject: Commerce

text: Which financial source is most appropriate for meeting a firm's short-term working capital needs?
explanation: A bank overdraft provides short-term, flexible funds to meet working capital needs; it allows withdrawal beyond account balance up to an agreed limit and is repayable on demand.
subject: Commerce

text: Which of the following is an example of indirect taxation?
explanation: Indirect taxes like VAT are collected by intermediaries (sellers) from buyers and passed to the government; they are levied on goods and services rather than on individual incomes directly.
subject: Commerce

text: If the domestic currency depreciates against foreign currencies, what is the immediate likely effect on imports?
options: Imports become cheaper in local currency
Imports become more expensive in local currency
explanation: Currency depreciation makes foreign goods cost more in domestic terms because more local currency is required to buy the same amount of foreign currency, increasing the local price of imports.
subject: Commerce

text: Which of the following is a trade barrier that directly restricts the quantity of goods allowed into a country?
explanation: A quota is a non-tariff barrier that sets a physical limit on the quantity of specific goods that may be imported into a country, directly restricting import volumes.
subject: Commerce

text: What is the principal purpose of licensing as a government control of business activities?
options: To regulate activity, protect consumers and maintain standards
explanation: Licensing allows government to control who may operate in certain trades, ensure compliance with standards, protect consumers and public interest, and regulate entry into sensitive industries.
subject: Commerce

text: Which document used in international trade provides a detailed statement of goods, their value and terms of sale between exporter and importer?
explanation: A commercial invoice is prepared by the exporter and details goods shipped, their prices, total value and terms of sale; it is essential for customs clearance and payment processes.
subject: Commerce

text: Who is the drawer of a bill of exchange?
options: The bank paying on behalf of the drawer
The person who orders the payment (creditor)
The person who accepts to pay the bill
The drawee who draws the bill on another
explanation: The drawer is the party that writes or draws the bill of exchange ordering the drawee to pay a specified sum to the payee; typically the creditor or seller draws the bill on the buyer.
subject: Commerce

text: Which party in a bill of exchange is primarily responsible for payment when the bill is presented?
explanation: The drawee is the person on whom the bill is drawn and who, upon accepting the bill, becomes primarily responsible for making payment to the payee when the bill matures.
subject: Commerce

text: A trader borrows N10,000 at simple interest rate of 5% per annum for 2 years. What is the interest payable?
explanation: Simple interest = Principal × Rate × Time = 10,000 × 0.05 × 2 = 1,000. Therefore interest payable over 2 years at 5% is N1,000, making this the correct option.
subject: Commerce

text: Which of the following best describes the role of advertising in marketing?
options: To inform and persuade potential customers about products
explanation: Advertising serves to inform consumers about product features, create awareness and persuade them to buy; it complements other marketing activities but does not replace personal selling entirely.
subject: Commerce

text: Which component of the marketing mix deals with how a product is distributed and where it is sold?
explanation: Place (distribution) concerns the channels and methods used to make products available to consumers, including physical locations, logistics, wholesalers and retailers.
subject: Commerce

text: Which of the following is a primary objective of consumer protection laws and agencies?
options: To punish all business owners indefinitely
To safeguard consumer rights, ensure safety and truthful information
explanation: Consumer protection aims to protect consumers from unsafe products, false advertising and unfair practices, ensuring safety, accurate information and redress mechanisms for grievances.
subject: Commerce

text: Which of the following actions would most likely improve a firm's liquidity position?
options: Converting current assets quickly into cash
Replacing current liabilities with long-term debt without changing assets
explanation: Improving liquidity is achieved by quickly converting current assets into cash or reducing short-term obligations; this increases the firm's ability to meet immediate liabilities and operating needs.
subject: Commerce

text: Which of the following best describes a public corporation?
options: Owned and controlled by the government to provide public services
A small partnership with family members only
An informal group without legal status
explanation: Public corporations are enterprises owned or controlled by the government, established to provide public goods or services, often with separate legal identity and statutory charters.
subject: Commerce

text: Which statement best describes a joint venture?
options: A long-term merger where two companies become one
A short-term collaboration between two or more parties for a specific project
An arrangement where employees own the company
A sole proprietorship that hires a partner temporarily
explanation: A joint venture involves two or more parties combining resources for a defined project or business activity, sharing risks, costs and profits for the specific venture before dissolution or extension.
subject: Commerce

text: Franchising as a form of business expansion typically involves:
options: The franchisor granting rights to a franchisee to use its brand and business model for a fee
Complete transfer of company ownership to customers
Free use of trademarks without any payment
explanation: In franchising, a franchisor allows a franchisee to operate using its brand, systems and support in return for initial fees and ongoing royalties, enabling rapid expansion with local operators.
subject: Commerce

text: Which of the following best defines working capital?
options: Funds used to purchase fixed assets like land and machinery
Net cash profit at the end of the year
Capital required for day-to-day running of business, measured by current assets minus current liabilities
explanation: Working capital is the capital needed for daily operations and expense payment; it equals current assets less current liabilities and indicates short-term financial health and operating efficiency.
subject: Commerce

text: Which scenario is an example of overstocking risk for a business?
options: Holding inventory beyond demand leading to increased storage costs and possible obsolescence
Running out of stock frequently and losing sales
Ordering too little stock to take advantage of bulk discounts
explanation: Overstocking means holding more inventory than demand requires, causing extra storage costs, capital tie-up, risk of spoilage or obsolescence and reduced liquidity for the business.
subject: Commerce

text: Which of the following best describes the role of middlemen in commerce?
options: They always manufacture goods before selling
They connect producers and consumers and provide services like breaking bulk, storage and risk bearing
They prevent goods from reaching the consumer
They collect taxes for the government
explanation: Middlemen (agents, wholesalers, retailers) bridge producers and consumers by facilitating distribution, providing storage, breaking bulk, bearing risk and often promoting and financing goods movement.
subject: Commerce

text: Which type of retailer specializes in narrow product lines and deep assortments, serving customers seeking expertise?
explanation: Specialty stores focus on a narrow product range with deep assortments and specialized service, attracting customers looking for expert advice and specific product varieties in that category.
subject: Commerce

text: Which security measure is most essential for safe online transactions in e-commerce?
options: Posting prices publicly on social media
Use of plain HTTP instead of HTTPS
explanation: Encryption protects data exchanged between buyer and seller by converting it into unreadable form for unauthorized parties, ensuring confidentiality and integrity of online transactions.
subject: Commerce

text: Which of the following is NOT normally considered a consumer right?
explanation: Consumer rights include safety, choice and accurate information; the 'right to be deceived' contradicts consumer protection principles and is never a recognized consumer right.
subject: Commerce

text: Which practice would best reflect good business ethics?
options: Concealing product defects to maintain sales
Falsifying financial records to show profit
Honest advertising and fair treatment of customers and employees
Ignoring laws to gain competitive advantage
explanation: Good business ethics involve honesty, fairness and compliance with laws: truthful advertising, fair treatment of stakeholders and integrity in transactions build reputation and sustainable success.
subject: Commerce

text: What does the break-even point for a business indicate?
options: Level of sales at which total revenue equals total cost with no profit or loss
A point where fixed costs are zero
The minimum wage payable to workers
explanation: Break-even point is where total revenues equal total costs, meaning the business neither makes profit nor incurs loss; it helps managers set sales targets needed to cover costs.
subject: Commerce

text: Which of the following is a negotiable instrument payable to bearer rather than to order?
explanation: A bearer cheque is payable to whoever presents it, making it negotiable by delivery. Order cheques and crossed or named payee cheques restrict transferability.
subject: Commerce

text: Which of the following best distinguishes a bank loan from an overdraft facility?
options: An overdraft is for a fixed long term while a loan is always short term
Loan provides a lump sum repayable on schedule; overdraft allows flexible short-term borrowing up to an agreed limit
Loans cannot be repaid; overdrafts are forgiven
Overdrafts are issued only to governments
explanation: Loans provide a specific sum repayable over fixed terms, while overdrafts allow current account holders to withdraw beyond their balance up to a limit for short-term liquidity with flexible repayment.
subject: Commerce

text: Which document issued by a warehouse acknowledges receipt of goods and may serve as a document of title?
explanation: A warehouse receipt is issued by the warehouse manager when goods are stored; it records possession and can be used as evidence of title or for raising finance against stored goods.
subject: Commerce

text: Which of the following factors would a business most likely consider when choosing a mode of transport?
options: Speed required, cost, nature of goods and distance
explanation: Choice of transport depends on practical factors like speed needs, cost, goods' nature (perishable or heavy), reliability and distance; irrelevant social factors do not determine choice.
subject: Commerce

text: Which of the following pairs correctly matches a shipping document with its primary purpose?
options: Packing list — shows insurance coverage details
Insurance policy — certifies country of origin
Certificate of origin — verifies goods' country of manufacture
Bill of lading — lists employees of the shipping company
explanation: A certificate of origin confirms where goods were produced, important for customs and preferential tariff treatment. Packing lists and bills of lading serve different specific purposes.
subject: Commerce

text: Which pricing strategy involves setting a low initial price to quickly penetrate the market and attract customers?
explanation: Penetration pricing sets low initial prices to attract customers, gain market share quickly and deter competitors; it contrasts with skimming which sets high initial prices to maximize margins.
subject: Commerce

text: Which of the following is a common reason governments provide subsidies to local producers?
options: To make imports cheaper than local goods
To support local industries, reduce production costs and encourage competitiveness
To punish local producers by increasing their taxes
explanation: Subsidies lower producers' costs, support infant industries, promote exports and improve competitiveness against imports; they are a form of government assistance to achieve economic objectives.
subject: Commerce

text: Which of these best describes 'trade credit' as a source of finance?
options: Short-term credit extended by suppliers allowing delayed payment
Bank loan collateralized by fixed assets
Sale of a company’s shares to the public
explanation: Trade credit is supplier-provided short-term financing where goods are delivered with payment deferred for an agreed period. It helps firms manage working capital without immediate cash outlay.
subject: Commerce

text: What is meant by the term 'commercial invoice' in export transactions?
options: A document prepared by the carrier to list passengers
A financial document from exporter stating goods sold, price, terms and total amount payable
An internal memo with staff attendance
A certificate issued by customs to allow import
explanation: A commercial invoice is issued by the exporter and states the goods sold, unit prices, total value and terms of sale; it is used for customs clearance and calculating duties and taxes.
subject: Commerce

text: Which of the following best explains the term 'market segmentation'?
options: Dividing a market into distinct groups of buyers with similar needs or characteristics
Combining all customers into one homogeneous group
Eliminating small customer groups to save costs
Setting different prices for the same product randomly
explanation: Market segmentation divides a market into groups of buyers with similar needs or characteristics, enabling firms to target products and marketing efforts more effectively to each segment.
subject: Commerce

text: Which action by a business would most directly improve its competitiveness in international markets?
options: Ignoring quality standards and reducing packaging
Improving product quality, complying with standards and reducing delivery times
Raising prices arbitrarily without value addition
Refusing to enter export documentation procedures
explanation: Competitiveness in international markets is improved by enhancing product quality, meeting international standards and ensuring timely delivery, which builds buyer confidence and strengthens market position.
subject: Commerce

text: Which of the following best explains 'subrogation' in insurance?
options: Insurer's right to pursue third parties after indemnifying the insured
A clause that cancels policy on expiry
A guarantee to always pay double the loss
Requirement for insured to under-declare assets
explanation: Subrogation allows the insurer, after indemnifying the insured for a loss, to step into the insured's shoes and recover the loss from any third party responsible for causing it, protecting insurer interests.
subject: Commerce

text: Which of the following best describes 'warehouse as agent' arrangement?
options: Warehouse acts on behalf of the owner and stores goods for sale, issuing warehouse receipts
Warehouse seizes goods and sells them without records
Warehouse manufactures goods on behalf of the owner
Warehouse refuses to accept any liability for goods stored
explanation: When a warehouse acts as agent, it stores goods on behalf of the owner, issues receipted documents (warehouse receipts) and can sell or release goods only according to the owner's instructions.
subject: Commerce

text: Which of the following best describes the effect of inflation on consumers' purchasing power?
options: Inflation increases purchasing power because prices fall
Inflation reduces purchasing power because the same money buys fewer goods
Inflation has no effect on purchasing power
Inflation only affects producers, not consumers
explanation: Inflation means a general rise in prices; as prices increase, the same amount of money buys fewer goods and services, thereby reducing consumers' real purchasing power over time.
subject: Commerce

text: Which of the following best explains 'subcontracting' in production and service delivery?
options: Hiring external firms to perform tasks the main firm cannot or chooses not to do
Combining two businesses into one legal entity
explanation: Subcontracting involves contracting out parts of production or services to external firms, allowing the main firm to access specialized skills, reduce costs or increase capacity without expanding internal resources.
subject: Commerce

text: Which of these is an advantage of registering a business (formal registration)?
options: Access to legal recognition, protection, ability to enter contracts and easier access to formal credit
Requirement to close business during holidays
explanation: Formal registration gives legal identity, enables contracting, provides limited liability protections (in some forms), improves credibility and makes it easier to obtain loans from formal lenders.
subject: Commerce
